rail_guard.text: Kent Station. Trains to every Irish station you have visited. Cork people call themselves the real capital. The trains, with a straight face, go along with it.
Hop aboard. The Wildlore rail runs to any town you have visited on this island. Where to?

market_fishmonger.text: Fresh off the boat this morning. Which boat? The boat. Don't ask for details, it's a trade secret.
The English Market's got a fountain with fish in it. That's the only place in the building where the fish are free.

bell_ringer.text: You can ring the Shandon bells yourself. There's a tune sheet, and a lot of enthusiasm. The tune will be recognisable. Possibly.
There's a golden salmon on top of the tower, as the weathervane. Cork's had a long relationship with fish.

rebel_local.text: We call ourselves 'Rebels', in Cork. It's the Rebel County. It's not a very dangerous thing. Mostly we rebel against other counties' accents.
Cork has its own sing-song accent, its own words, and a lot of pride in both. It's very affectionate. You'll find yourself copying it by teatime.

lee_swimmer.text: The Lee runs both sides of the city, and the people go on both. It's quite the commute. Mind the swans, they know where the bread is.
Cork Harbour, at the end of the river, is one of the biggest natural harbours in the world. A sailor's dream. A swimmer's disagreement.

kent_stationman.text: Kent Station's named for Thomas Kent, a Cork man executed after the 1916 Rising. It used to be called Glanmire Road. People still call it that, to be safe.
I'm collecting every train that comes through. So far it's been thirteen. I'm told that's a low number for a day.
